fields.mechanism: Application of vacuum through internal lumens to establish a controlled pressure gradient that drives fluid flow, as described by Darcy's law.
fields.intervention: Integrate a distributed vacuum-assist manifold along the multi-lumen medical tubing that applies localized negative pressure through dedicated auxiliary lumens, establishing a longitudinal pressure gradient to actively drive fluid and counteract viscous friction losses without requiring higher upstream positive pressures or altering the primary lumen geometry.
fields.expected_effect: The applied pressure gradient offsets viscous friction losses within the tubing, reducing net pressure loss while preserving the original wall thickness, kink resistance, and lumen patency because no geometric changes to the primary flow path are required.
fields.falsification_test: Measure the differential pressure drop across a 1-meter length of the modified multi-lumen tubing at a constant flow rate with the vacuum manifold deactivated versus activated; if the pressure drop does not decrease by at least 15% when activated while maintaining identical kink-resistance per ASTM F2376, the mechanism fails.
fields.mechanism_source_span: The hollow microneedle approach retains the microneedles in the skin and applies vacuum through internal lumens, allowing integration of the vacuum source, microneedles, and biosensors into a single wearable platform for in situ biomarker detection.

fields.mechanism: Passive pressure gradient flow through a porous medium governed by Darcy's law, inverted by removing the active vacuum source and relying on the intrinsic fluid pressure differential to drive flow while using the structural matrix as a passive kink-resistant scaffold.
fields.intervention: Replace smooth inner lumen walls with a rigid, microporous structural liner analogous to the dermal extracellular matrix, utilizing the natural arterial-venous or infusion-site pressure differential as the sole driving force instead of external pumping, thereby maintaining patency via the rigid porous architecture without requiring active suction.
fields.expected_effect: The rigid microporous liner prevents lumen collapse under bending loads, maintaining kink resistance and patency, while the distributed porous structure eliminates localized high-velocity boundary layers, reducing overall viscous pressure loss compared to conventional smooth-bore tubing subjected to partial occlusion.
fields.falsification_test: Measure pressure drop across a 1-meter length of microporous-lined multi-lumen tubing at physiological flow rates (e.g., 500 mL/min) while bent to a 15 mm radius; if the pressure drop exceeds that of a standard smooth-bore tube at the same bend radius, or if the lumen cross-sectional area decreases by more than 5%, the mechanism fails.
fields.mechanism_source_span: This review reframes dermal ISF sampling as a pressure gradient engineering problem using Darcy's law.

fields.expected_effect: Reduced net pressure loss across the tubing length without altering the physical wall thickness or lumen diameter, maintaining kink resistance and lumen patency
fields.falsification_test: Measure the differential pressure between the inlet and outlet of the multi-lumen tubing at a constant volumetric flow rate with and without applied proximal vacuum; if the pressure drop does not decrease by at least 10% under vacuum, the mechanism fails to address the failure

fields.mechanism: Vacuum-assisted pressure gradient driving fluid flow through internal lumens combined with structural retention of hollow conduits to maintain pathway integrity
fields.intervention: Integrate a distributed micro-vacuum manifold along the multi-lumen tubing wall that applies a controlled negative pressure gradient through dedicated auxiliary lumens (fluidic domain) while utilizing the rigid hollow microneedle-like structural geometry of these vacuum lumens as internal anti-collapse struts (mechanical domain), thereby actively offsetting viscous pressure loss via Darcy's law without relying solely on passive lumen diameter
fields.expected_effect: Reduction in net pressure loss across the tubing length due to active vacuum-driven flow assistance, while kink resistance and lumen patency are maintained or improved by the structural reinforcement provided by the retained hollow vacuum lumens acting as internal mechanical supports
fields.falsification_test: Measure the pressure drop across a 1-meter length of prototype multi-lumen tubing at a fixed flow rate with the vacuum manifold activated versus deactivated, and simultaneously perform a mandrel kink test per ASTM F640 to verify that the radius at which flow occludes does not decrease compared to standard tubing lacking the vacuum lumens

fields.mechanism: Pressure gradient engineering using Darcy's law to drive fluid flow through a resistive medium without increasing the conduit's structural rigidity
fields.intervention: Apply a controlled vacuum (negative pressure) at the distal outlet of the multi-lumen medical tubing to establish an axial pressure gradient that drives fluid, rather than relying solely on proximal positive pressure pushing against viscous resistance
fields.expected_effect: Reduces the required proximal driving pressure for a target flow rate, decreasing the transmural pressure differential across the tube wall and thereby preserving lumen patency and kink resistance while mitigating net pressure loss along the length
fields.falsification_test: Measure flow rate versus applied proximal pressure in a standard multi-lumen tube with and without a fixed distal vacuum; if the vacuum-assisted configuration does not yield a higher flow rate at the same proximal pressure or equivalent flow at lower proximal pressure, the mechanism fails
